title: Chebe powder: length retention, growth claims and safety
question_forms: How do I use chebe powder?
tradition_says: Chebe powder is said to stop breakage so hair grows very long, and is applied to the hair lengths under braids; families and online communities swear by it.

layer1.plain_answer: Chebe is a traditional herbal hair powder, mixed with oil or butter and coated on the lengths. My search found no study of it on hair or in people. A doctor quoted by PureWow says it does not grow hair. Any benefit is untested, so patch test first and avoid heavy coating on thin strands.

do.text: Patch test first, since its side effects are unknown.

source.name: PureWow, "Chebe powder for hair" (quotes Dr Sunitha Posina, an internist, and two hair professionals)

do.text: Use it as a conditioning treatment on the lengths: a stylist suggests a weekly treatment left on for at least an hour.

source.name: PureWow, "Chebe powder for hair" (quotes Dr Sunitha Posina, an internist, and two hair professionals)

avoid.text: Heavy application on thin or fine strands: a stylist warns it is heavy and can cause breakage.

source.name: PureWow, "Chebe powder for hair" (quotes Dr Sunitha Posina, an internist, and two hair professionals)

avoid.text: Expecting hair growth: Dr Sunitha Posina says there is no evidence it grows hair.

source.name: PureWow, "Chebe powder for hair" (quotes Dr Sunitha Posina, an internist, and two hair professionals)

see_someone_when: Itching, a rash or burning on your scalp after using it (doctor or dermatologist).
Thinning at the hairline or temples, whatever you use (doctor or dermatologist; ask about traction).
Hair breaking despite careful care (doctor or a hair and scalp specialist).

tier_driver: That chebe stops breakage or grows hair: my search found no study in people or on hair; one internist quoted by a magazine says it has no evidence behind it.
tier_note: D because the claim people make has no human or lab evidence in what I opened. It would move if a study measured breakage or length on afro-textured hair with and without chebe.
harm_note: No harm study found. PureWow quotes a doctor saying its side effects are unknown and advising a patch test, and a stylist warning it is heavy on thin strands. A Reddit thread reviewed by the practices layer reports an itchy rash when it touched the scalp (forum report only, not counted as evidence).
evidence_summary: My searches found no study of chebe powder. PubMed returned 7 records for the bare word 'chebe' (none about hair) and none for Croton or Basara hair; the positive control 'Khumalo NP AND hair' returned 71 results, so the search works. ClinicalTrials.gov returned no chebe study. A PureWow article quotes an internist who says chebe does not grow hair and that there are no peer-reviewed studies, and a cosmetologist who lists its ingredients as local tree resin, cherry seeds, lavender and cloves.
measured_variables: Hair breakage and length retained (untested for chebe)
gaps: Untested: everything. No study of chebe on hair strength, breakage, length or growth, in afro-textured hair or any hair; no analysis of what is in commercial chebe products; allergy rates. The only source is one magazine article, not a clinical source. Origin (Basara women in Chad) is described in the practices layer only from a search summary and is not used here. The ingredient question (a herb or food) sits with Food's herbal entries; this entry is in Hair because the use is on hair.
